BD.BTRA2001.s97A.text: The Government may, in the interest of the security of the State or public order, direct the suspension or interception of telecommunication services, and any such direction shall be issued by the authority empowered by the Government for that purpose.

BD.CPP.WARNING.text: The Cyclone Preparedness Programme shall disseminate cyclone warning signals issued by the Bangladesh Meteorological Department to coastal communities through its network of volunteers using megaphones, flags and sirens, in Bengali, and shall continue dissemination until the danger signal is withdrawn.

BD.DMA2012.s24.text: On receipt of an early warning of an impending disaster, the Deputy Commissioner of the district concerned shall activate the district disaster management committee and shall cause the warning to be disseminated to the inhabitants of the areas likely to be affected through all available means without delay.

BD.SOD2019.ptd.section: Posts and Telecommunications Division / BTRC / BTCL responsibilities (pp. 240-246)
BD.SOD2019.ptd.text: The Posts and Telecommunications Division, the Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulatory Commission and BTCL are assigned responsibilities for maintaining and restoring telecommunication services during a disaster, including keeping emergency communication available to the disaster management authorities. Page range per the SOD table of contents; extract and quote the actual pages before citing.

IN.CERTIN2022.p2.instrument: CERT-In Directions under s.70B(6) IT Act, 28 April 2022 (India)
IN.CERTIN2022.p2.text: Any service provider, intermediary, data centre, body corporate and Government organisation shall mandatorily report cyber incidents of the types specified in Annexure I to CERT-In within six hours of noticing such incidents or being brought to notice about such incidents.

IN.DMA2005.s22.2.h.text: The State Executive Committee shall give directions to any department of the Government of the State or any other authority or body in the State regarding actions to be taken in response to any threatening disaster situation or disaster, and shall advise the State Government regarding all financial matters in relation to disaster management.

IN.DMA2005.s34.c.text: For the purpose of assisting and protecting the community affected by a disaster, the District Authority may give directions for the release and use of resources available with any department of the Government and the local authority in the district, and may ensure that warnings and alerts are communicated to the public in the affected area.

IN.DMA2005.s6.text: The National Disaster Management Authority shall have the responsibility for laying down the policies, plans and guidelines for disaster management and for coordinating their enforcement and implementation throughout the country, and shall lay down guidelines to be followed by the departments or agencies of the Government of India.

IN.DOTSOP2020.committees.instrument: DoT Standard Operating Procedure 2020 for Telecommunication Services for responding to Disasters (India)
IN.DOTSOP2020.committees.text: A national committee chaired by Member (Technology) oversees telecom disaster response, with corresponding committees at licensed service area (circle) level, nodal officers designated by each telecom service provider, and damage-assessment teams. Content per secondary reporting; verify against the SOP before quoting.

IN.DOTSOP2020.icr.instrument: DoT Standard Operating Procedure 2020 for Telecommunication Services for responding to Disasters (India)
IN.DOTSOP2020.icr.text: Intra-circle roaming during a disaster is to be arranged through mutual agreement between telecom service providers, pursuant to memoranda of understanding entered into between them, rather than by a standing regulatory trigger. Activation is requested through the designated DoT disaster official. Dated 14 December 2020. Content per secondary reporting; verify against the SOP before quoting.

IN.DPDP2023.s2.instrument: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act 22 of 2023)
IN.DPDP2023.s2.text: 2. In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires,— (a) “Appellate Tribunal” means the Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal established under section 14 of the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India Act, 1997; (b) “automated” means any digital process capable of operating automatically in response to instructions given or otherwise for the purpose of processing data; (c) “Board” means the Data Protection Board of India established by the Central Government under section 18; (d) “certain legitimate uses” means the uses referred to in section 7; (e) “Chairperson” means the Chairperson of the Board; (f) “child” means an individual who has not completed the age of eighteen years; (g) “Consent Manager” means a person registered with the Board, who acts as a single point of contact to enable a Data Principal to give, manage, review and withdraw her consent through an accessible, transparent and interoperable platform; (h) “data” means a representation of information, facts, concepts, opinions or instructions in a manner suitable for communication, interpretation or processing by human beings or by automated means; (i) “Data Fiduciary” means any person who alone or in conjunction with other persons determines the purpose and means of processing of personal data; (j) “Data Principal” means the individual to whom the personal data relates and where such individual is— (i) a child, includes the parents or lawful guardian of such a child; (ii) a person with disability, includes her lawful guardian, acting on her behalf; (k) “Data Processor” means any person who processes personal data on behalf of a Data Fiduciary; (l) “Data Protection Officer” means an individual appointed by the Significant Data Fiduciary under clause (a) of sub-section (2) of section 10; (m) “digital office” means an office that adopts an online mechanism wherein the proceedings, from receipt of intimation or complaint or reference or directions or appeal, as the case may be, to the disposal thereof, are conducted in online or digital mode; (n) “digital personal data” means personal data in digital form; (o) “gain” means— (i) a gain in property or supply of services, whether temporary or permanent; or (ii) an opportunity to earn remuneration or greater remuneration or to gain a financial advantage otherwise than by way of legitimate remuneration; (p) “loss” means— (i) a loss in property or interruption in supply of services, whether temporary or permanent; or (ii) a loss of opportunity to earn remuneration or greater remuneration or to gain a financial advantage otherwise than by way of legitimate remuneration; (q) “Member” means a Member of the Board and includes the Chairperson; (r) “notification” means a notification published in the Official Gazette and the expressions “notify” and “notified” shall be construed accordingly; (s) “person” includes— (i) an individual; (ii) a Hindu undivided family; (iii) a company; (iv) a firm; (v) an association of persons or a body of individuals, whether incorporated or not; (vi) the State; and (vii) every artificial juristic person, not falling within any of the preceding sub-clauses; (t) “personal data” means any data about an individual who is identifiable by or in relation to such data; (u) “personal data breach” means any unauthorised processing of personal data or accidental disclosure, acquisition, sharing, use, alteration, destruction or loss of access to personal data, that compromises the confidentiality, integrity or availability of personal data; (v) “prescribed” means prescribed by rules made under this Act; (w) “proceeding” means any action taken by the Board under the provisions of this Act; (x) “processing” in relation to personal data, means a wholly or partly automated operation or set of operations performed on digital personal data, and includes operations such as collection, recording, organisation, structuring, storage, adaptation, retrieval, use, alignment or combination, indexing, sharing, disclosure by transmission, dissemination or otherwise making available, restriction, erasure or destruction; (y) “she” in relation to an individual includes the reference to such individual irrespective of gender; (z) “Significant Data Fiduciary” means any Data Fiduciary or class of Data Fiduciaries as may be notified by the Central Government under section 10; (za) “specified purpose” means the purpose mentioned in the notice given by the Data Fiduciary to the Data Principal in accordance with the provisions of this Act and the rules made thereunder; and (zb) “State” means the State as defined under article 12 of the Constitution.

IN.DPDP2023.s27.instrument: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act 22 of 2023)
IN.DPDP2023.s27.text: 27. (1) The Board shall exercise and perform the following powers and functions, namely:— (a) on receipt of an intimation of personal data breach under sub-section (6) of section 8, to direct any urgent remedial or mitigation measures in the event of a personal data breach, and to inquire into such personal data breach and impose penalty as provided in this Act; (b) on a complaint made by a Data Principal in respect of a personal data breach or a breach in observance by a Data Fiduciary of its obligations in relation to her personal data or the exercise of her rights under the provisions of this Act, or on a reference made to it by the Central Government or a State Government, or in compliance of the directions of any court, to inquire into such breach and impose penalty as provided in this Act; (c) on a complaint made by a Data Principal in respect of a breach in observance by a Consent Manager of its obligations in relation to her personal data, to inquire into such breach and impose penalty as provided in this Act; (d) on receipt of an intimation of breach of any condition of registration of a Consent Manager, to inquire into such breach and impose penalty as provided in this Act; and (e) on a reference made by the Central Government in respect of the breach in observance of the provisions of sub-section (2) of section 37 by an intermediary, to inquire into such breach and impose penalty as provided in this Act. (2) The Board may, for the effective discharge of its functions under the provisions of this Act, after giving the person concerned an opportunity of being heard and after recording reasons in writing, issue such directions as it may consider necessary to such person, who shall be bound to comply with the same. (3) The Board may, on a representation made to it by a person affected by a direction issued under sub-section (1) or sub-section (2), or on a reference made by the Central Government, modify, suspend, withdraw or cancel such direction and, while doing so, impose such conditions as it may deem fit, subject to which the modification, suspension, withdrawal or cancellation shall have effect. Procedure to be followed by Board.

IN.IMD.CYCWARN.instrument: IMD Cyclone Warning Services standard operating procedure (India)
IN.IMD.CYCWARN.text: The India Meteorological Department issues cyclone warnings in four stages: Pre-Cyclone Watch, Cyclone Alert, Cyclone Warning, and Post-Landfall Outlook, addressed to the State Governments and disaster management authorities of the areas likely to be affected, with the Cyclone Warning stage issued at least twenty-four hours before expected commencement of adverse weather.

IN.NDMA.CAP.SACHET.instrument: NDMA Common Alerting Protocol / SACHET Integrated Alert System (India)
IN.NDMA.CAP.SACHET.text: The Common Alerting Protocol based Integrated Alert System disseminates disaster warnings issued by designated alerting authorities to the public in the affected area over multiple channels including cell broadcast and SMS, in English, Hindi and the relevant regional language, with the alerting authority responsible for the area accountable for issuing the alert.

IN.SUSP2024.r2.1.text: Directions to suspend telecommunication services shall not be issued except by an order made by the Secretary to the Government of India in the Ministry of Home Affairs in the case of the Central Government, or by the Secretary to the State Government in charge of the Home Department in the case of a State Government, who is hereby designated as the competent authority.

IN.SUSP2024.r2.2.text: In unavoidable circumstances where obtaining prior direction of the competent authority is not feasible, such direction may be issued by an officer not below the rank of Joint Secretary to the Government of India who has been duly authorised by the competent authority, and such direction shall cease to be in effect unless confirmed by the competent authority within twenty-four hours of its issue.

IN.SUSP2024.r2.3.text: Every order issued directing suspension of telecommunication services shall contain reasons for such direction, shall specify the area and duration of suspension, and a copy of such order shall be forwarded to the concerned Review Committee not later than the next working day.

IN.SUSP2024.r2.4.text: Any direction for suspension of telecommunication services shall not remain in operation for more than fifteen days at a time, and a fresh order shall be required to continue the suspension beyond that period.

IN.SUSP2024.r2.5.text: The Review Committee shall meet within five working days of the issue of a direction for suspension of telecommunication services and shall record its findings on whether the direction is in accordance with the governing provisions of law.

IN.SUSP2024.r3.text: The authorised entity shall designate a nodal officer in each licensed service area to receive and handle directions for suspension of telecommunication services, and no direction shall be acted upon unless it is received through the designated nodal officer channel.

IN.TA2023.s20.2.text: (2) On the occurrence of any public emergency or in the interest of public safety, the Central Government or a State Government or any officer specially authorised in this behalf by the Central Government or a State Government, may, if satisfied that it is necessary or expedient so to do, in the interest of the sovereignty and integrity of India, defence and security of the State, friendly relations with foreign States, public order, or for preventing incitement to the commission of any offence, subject to such procedure and safeguards as may be prescribed, and for reasons to be recorded in writing, by order— (a) direct that any message or class of messages, to or from any person or class of persons, to or from any telecommunication equipment or class of telecommunication equipment, or relating to any particular subject, brought for Provisions for public emergency or public safety. transmission by, or transmitted or received by any telecommunication service or telecommunication network, shall not be transmitted, or shall be intercepted or detained, or shall be disclosed in intelligible format to the officer mentioned in such order; or (b) direct that any telecommunication service or class of telecommunication services to or from any person or class of persons, to or from any telecommunication equipment or class of telecommunication equipment, or relating to any particular subject, transmitted or received by any telecommunication service or telecommunication network, shall be suspended.

IN.TA2023.s23.text: 23. If it appears necessary or expedient so to do in the public interest, the Central Government may direct any authorised entity to transmit in its telecommunication services or telecommunication network, specific messages, in such manner as may be specified. Power to give directions. DIGITAL BHARAT NIDHI 13 of 1885.

(A) for the words and figures "Indian Telegraph Act, 1885", the words, figures and brackets "Telecommunications Act, 2023 or the Cable Television Networks (Regulation) Act, 1995" shall be substituted; (B) in the fifth proviso, for the portion beginning with the words "may, within fifteen days from the date of receipt" and ending with the words "take a final decision", the following shall be substituted, namely:— "shall, within thirty days from the date of receipt of such reference communicate to the Central Government any further recommendations that it may have, after considering the reference made by the Central Government and after receipt of further recommendation if any, the Central Government shall take a final decision."; (ii) in sub-section (2),— 13 of 1885. (A) for the words and figures "Indian Telegraph Act, 1885", the words, figures and brackets "Telecommunications Act, 2023 or the Cable Television Networks (Regulation) Act, 1995" shall be substituted; (B) after the proviso, the following proviso shall be inserted, namely:— "Provided further that the Authority may direct an authorised entity or class of authorised entities providing telecommunication services, to abstain from predatory pricing that is harmful to competition, long term development and the overall health of the telecommunication sector."; (d) in section 14, in clause (a),— (i) sub-clause (i) shall be omitted; (ii) for paragraph (C), the following shall be substituted, namely:— "(C) any disputes to be adjudicated by the Adjudicating Officer or the Designated Appeals Committee under the Telecommunications Act, 2023; (iii) after clause (c), the following clause shall be inserted, namely:— "(d) hear and dispose of appeals under section 39 of the Telecommunications Act, 2023. Any action instituted under the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India Act, 1997 and pending immediately before the appointed day in the Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal, shall continue to be heard and disposed of by the Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal as if this Act had not been passed;"; (e) for section 38, the following section shall be substituted, namely:— Application of certain laws. "38. The provisions of this Act shall be in addition to the provisions of the Telecommunications Act, 2023 and, in particular, nothing in this Act shall affect any jurisdiction, powers and functions required to be exercised or performed by the appropriate authority in relation to any area falling within the jurisdiction of such authority.". REPEAL AND SAVINGS Repeal of certain Acts and savings.

IN.TCSR2024.no_order_auth.text: NEGATIVE FINDING, not a quotation. The Telecom Cyber Security Rules 2024 impose incident-reporting duties on authorised entities but, on secondary reporting of the notified text, contain no requirement that an authorised entity authenticate the provenance of a direction or order received from a government officer before giving effect to it. This record exists so the policy engine can cite the absence of such a duty. It must be confirmed against the full notified text before the report asserts it.

INTL.ITU.X1303.instrument: ITU-T Recommendation X.1303, Common Alerting Protocol (CAP 1.1)
INTL.ITU.X1303.text: The Common Alerting Protocol provides an open, non-proprietary digital message format for all types of alerts and notifications, specifying an alert message structure with alert, info, resource and area blocks, where the info block carries the language, category, urgency, severity and certainty of the alert and the area block carries the geographic scope.

INTL.TAMPERE1998.art3.instrument: Tampere Convention on the Provision of Telecommunication Resources for Disaster Mitigation and Relief Operations, 1998
INTL.TAMPERE1998.art3.text: The States Parties shall cooperate among themselves and with non-State entities and intergovernmental organizations to facilitate the use of telecommunication resources for disaster mitigation and relief, including the deployment of terrestrial and satellite telecommunication equipment to predict, monitor and provide information concerning natural hazards and disasters. Party status of individual States must be verified on the UN Treaty Collection before being encoded in a policy pack (see spec section 14).

INTL.TAMPERE1998.art4.instrument: Tampere Convention on the Provision of Telecommunication Resources for Disaster Mitigation and Relief Operations, 1998
INTL.TAMPERE1998.art4.text: A State Party requiring telecommunication assistance for disaster mitigation and relief may request such assistance from any other State Party, and the requested State Party shall promptly determine and notify the requesting State Party whether it will render the assistance requested, directly or otherwise, and the scope of and terms on which such assistance might be rendered.

flow.body: Every instrument is fetched once, hashed, and checked against strings only the real document carries. A source we do not hold says so, and names the finding it caps.
flow.title: Primary sources

flow.body: Gazette PDFs are split clause by clause. Each record keeps its verbatim text, a sha256 of that text, the page, and the hash of the PDF it came from.
flow.title: Ingest

flow.body: One chunk per clause, each carrying clause_id, instrument, jurisdiction, page and source_url -- so a hit can be cited, not just quoted.
flow.title: Structure and retrieval

flow.body: A rule that cites a clause the store does not hold, or whose text no longer hashes as recorded, does not compile. The simulator cannot run on invented law.
flow.title: Policy packs

flow.body: Each agent sees only its own inbox, delayed and redacted, and returns a typed proposal naming the rule it believes authorises it.
flow.title: Agents propose

flow.body: A pure function over (proposal, world, pack). No model appears anywhere in its import graph, and a test fails the build if one ever does.
flow.title: The engine decides

flow.body: One world state, one rulebook, one fixed order: (t, role priority, proposal_id). This is what makes the same seed produce the same ledger head hash.
flow.title: The Game Master resolves

flow.body: Every entry commits to the one before it. The four properties are checked against the finished world, and a budget of 300 mutated worlds is searched for the minimal case.
flow.title: Ledger and findings

gaps.domain_gap: Emergency telecom: A suspension direction carries no mandatory carve-out for relief and emergency traffic, and priority routing is permitted rather than obliged, so a lawful suspension can switch off the very traffic the response depends on.

gaps.itu_hook: ITU-T E.106 International Emergency Preference Scheme
gaps.neighbour_instance: Bangladesh (BTRA 2001 + DM Act 2012 + CPP standing order): PASSES the same seed

gaps.domain_gap: Emergency telecom: No instrument requires an operator to authenticate a service-suspension direction before giving effect to it, so a forged direction executes exactly like a genuine one and the irreversible act is complete before any verification occurs.
gaps.global_example: United States (FCC Mandatory Disaster Response Initiative + DIRS): PASSES the same seed
gaps.neighbour_instance: Bangladesh (BTRA 2001 + DM Act 2012 + CPP standing order): PASSES the same seed

gaps.domain_gap: Emergency telecom: No standing cross-border trigger: no instrument empowers any actor to issue a public alert across the border in time, and the domestic alerting/roaming power is scoped to domestic areas only.
gaps.global_example: United States (FCC Mandatory Disaster Response Initiative + DIRS): PASSES the same seed
gaps.neighbour_instance: Bangladesh (BTRA 2001 + DM Act 2012 + CPP standing order): PASSES the same seed

gaps.domain_gap: Emergency telecom: No standing cross-border trigger: no instrument empowers any actor to enable disaster roaming across the border in time, and the domestic alerting/roaming power is scoped to domestic areas only.
gaps.global_example: United States (FCC Mandatory Disaster Response Initiative + DIRS): PASSES the same seed
gaps.itu_hook: ITU-D Guidelines for National Emergency Telecommunication Plans
gaps.neighbour_instance: Bangladesh (BTRA 2001 + DM Act 2012 + CPP standing order): also fails (coordination gap)

gaps.domain_gap: Emergency telecom: disaster roaming has no standing, automatically triggered obligation; it is arranged between operators and switched on by request, so the clock starts only once somebody asks.
gaps.evidence: documents: IN.DOTSOP2020.icr IN.UL.DISASTER; reproduced as P4 on run amphan_2020__india_current__rule__seed0
gaps.global_example: 47 CFR 4.17 makes roaming-under-disaster-arrangements a standing obligation on a provider whose network is impaired, triggered by the event rather than by a request. [US.CFR47.4.17.trigger* US.CFR47.4.17.a* US.FCC.DIRS*]
gaps.india_instance: DoT SOP-2020 routes intra-circle roaming through MoUs between TSPs on mutually agreed terms; activation is requested through DoT rather than triggered by the disaster itself. [IN.DOTSOP2020.icr* IN.UL.DISASTER*]
gaps.itu_hook: ITU-D Guidelines for National Emergency Telecommunication Plans (2020)
gaps.neighbour_instance: Bhutan's SOP for Telecom Services during Disaster contains no roaming provision at all. [BT.TELSOP.no_roaming*]

gaps.domain_gap: Emergency telecom: a national emergency telecommunication plan is not operational, so disaster-time telecom coordination rests on standing committees rather than on a plan with owners and deadlines.
gaps.global_example: The ITU-D guidelines set out what an NETP contains and who owns each part of it. [INTL.ITU.NETP2020*]
gaps.india_instance: SOP-2020 establishes committees and nodal officers; it is an SOP, not a costed national plan. [IN.DOTSOP2020.committees*]
gaps.itu_hook: ITU-D NETP Guidelines; ITU target of an NETP in every country
gaps.neighbour_instance: Bangladesh's National Emergency Telecommunication Service initiative has run since Sep 2022 with funds available and, as reported, no plan in place. [BD.NETS.gap*]

gaps.domain_gap: Emergency telecom: orders to operators are not cryptographically authenticated, so a forged direction is indistinguishable from a genuine one at the moment the operator must act.
gaps.evidence: documents: IN.SUSP2024.r3 IN.TCSR2024.no_order_auth IN.TA2023.s20.2; reproduced as P2 on run amphan_2020__india_current__rule__seed0
gaps.global_example: ITU-T Q.3057 standardises certificate-based authentication of calling identity in signalling. There is no equivalent recommendation for authenticating an emergency order to an operator -- the standards gap is the absence, not a weaker alternative. [INTL.ITU.Q3057*]
gaps.india_instance: The Suspension Rules route a direction to a nodal officer by electronic means; neither they nor the Telecom Cyber Security Rules impose a duty to verify where it came from. [IN.SUSP2024.r3* IN.TCSR2024.no_order_auth* IN.TA2023.s20.2]
gaps.neighbour_instance: none found in the instruments held for Bangladesh, Bhutan or Bangladesh SOD 2019

gaps.domain_gap: Emergency telecom: suspension safeguards carry no mandatory carve-out for response and relief traffic, so a lawful suspension can switch off the traffic the response depends on.
gaps.evidence: documents: IN.TA2023.s20.1 IN.TA2023.s20.2 IN.SUSP2024.r2.1; reproduced as P1 on run amphan_2020__india_current__rule__seed0
gaps.global_example: E.106 and ITU Constitution Art. 40 give safety-of-life traffic absolute priority on international services. EU EECC Art. 110 is NOT cited: we hold no text for it. [INTL.ITU.E106* INTL.ITU.CONST.art40*]
gaps.india_instance: s.20(1)(b) ENABLES priority routing for authorised responders; it does not oblige it, and the 2024 Rules' safeguards address duration, review and who may order -- not a carve-out. [IN.TA2023.s20.1 IN.TA2023.s20.2 IN.SUSP2024.r2.1*]
gaps.itu_hook: ITU-T E.106 International Emergency Preference Scheme
gaps.neighbour_instance: Bangladesh's CPP standing order keeps the warning chain running independently of any suspension, which is why the same seed passes under the Bangladesh pack. [BD.CPP.WARNING*]

gaps.domain_gap: Emergency telecom: outage duration is set by site power backup, and no instrument states a numeric backup requirement, so the recovery clock is an engineering accident.
gaps.global_example: 47 CFR 4.17 obliges mutual aid and asset sharing between providers, which is a different lever on the same failure: it shortens outage without specifying a battery. [US.CFR47.4.17.b*]
gaps.india_instance: Neither the SOP nor the licence condition we hold states a minimum backup duration; the Amphan outages were driven by grid loss (COAI, as reported). [IN.DOTSOP2020.icr* IN.UL.DISASTER*]
gaps.neighbour_instance: Bangladesh SOD 2019 assigns PTD/BTRC/BTCL duties; tower batteries reported at 4-8 h. [BD.SOD2019.ptd*]

gaps.domain_gap: Emergency telecom: disaster telecom SOPs carry no numeric timelines, so "immediately" is the only deadline and nothing is measurable after the event.
gaps.global_example: 47 CFR 4.17 sets a 60-day reporting deadline and an annual roaming test; DIRS sets the reporting cadence during the event. [US.CFR47.4.17.b* US.FCC.DIRS*]
gaps.india_instance: SOP-2020 as held: committees, nodal officers and reporting, no numeric deadline. [IN.DOTSOP2020.committees* IN.DOTSOP2020.icr*]
gaps.neighbour_instance: Bhutan's SOP as held: "immediately" plus daily reporting. [BT.TELSOP.no_roaming*]

gaps.domain_gap: Emergency telecom: cross-border alerting has no defined path, so a CAP alert cannot reach the population on the far side of a border that the same cyclone is about to cross.
gaps.evidence: documents: IN.NDMA.CAP.SACHET IN.DMA2005.s6; reproduced as P3 on run amphan_2020__india_current__rule__seed0
gaps.global_example: X.1303 already carries multilingual, polygon-scoped alerts across any boundary; the gap is institutional, not technical. Tampere Art. 9 addresses regulatory barriers to relief telecoms. Party status per country is NOT asserted: we hold no treaty-status page. [INTL.ITU.X1303* INTL.TAMPERE1998.art9*]
gaps.india_instance: SACHET's CAP feeds are national and state-scoped; the alerting power is domestic. [IN.NDMA.CAP.SACHET* IN.DMA2005.s6*]
gaps.neighbour_instance: Bangladesh's warning chain runs on BMD cyclone signals through CPP volunteers -- a different channel, with no defined interface to SACHET. [BD.CPP.WARNING* BD.SOD2019.ptd*]

roles.analogue: Union/State Home Secretary under Telecom Act 2023 s.20 + Suspension Rules 2024
roles.boundaries: You do not see cell-level telemetry and you cannot verify a report yourself. You cannot operate the network; you can only order.
roles.mandate: Maintain public order and public safety while keeping the State's emergency response functioning. You answer for both an unnecessary suspension and a failure to act.
roles.name: Competent Authority (Home Department)

roles.analogue: NDMA/SDMA under DM Act 2005, CAP alerts via SACHET
roles.boundaries: You do not see network telemetry or cyber incidents. You cannot compel an operator to do anything.
roles.mandate: Get an accurate, intelligible warning to every person in every area at risk, in a language they read, before the hazard arrives.
roles.name: State Disaster Management Authority (alerting)

roles.boundaries: You do not receive meteorological warnings directly and you cannot verify whether an order you received is genuine. You cannot issue public alerts.
roles.mandate: Keep the network carrying traffic, above all emergency and relief traffic, and comply with lawful directions you receive through your nodal officer.
roles.name: Telecom Service Provider NOC (5G network and services)

roles.analogue: CERT-In, Directions of 28 April 2022, six-hour reporting
roles.boundaries: You see incident reports only. You do not see meteorological warnings, damage reports or public alerts, and you cannot order anything on the network.
roles.mandate: Detect and call out forged or tampered directions and reportable cyber incidents affecting telecom networks.
roles.name: CERT-In (national computer emergency response team)

roles.analogue: Bangladesh regulator / Department of Disaster Management
roles.boundaries: You reach everything through the cross-border channel, which is slow. You cannot see the other State's internal orders or telemetry.
roles.mandate: Protect the population on your side of the border. You act on your own legal powers, not on a foreign authority's order.
roles.name: Neighbouring State authority

roles.analogue: Standing legal/policy adviser to the response
roles.boundaries: Advisory only. Every claim must cite a clause_id present in the retrieved context. If the clauses do not answer the question, say so and name the gap.
roles.mandate: Answer questions about who may lawfully do what, citing clauses. You hold no powers and you propose no actions.
roles.name: Policy & Legal Adviser

y3172.description: Data source: acts, rules, registers, scenario definitions
members: Replay a mutation list onto the base scenario. This is what makes a FailureCard reproducible.
Add latency to one role's channel. This is the mutation that manufactures coordination gaps.
Delay one fact for one role: the finest-grained way to make information uneven.
Add a damage report for an area, which also marks that area affected.
Add an order no authority issued. `authentic=False` is ground truth no agent can read.
Add an unverified claim visible to the competent authority. No world effect by construction.
Move one event in time. Release order changes, so who-knows-what-when changes with it.
Load and validate a scenario YAML. Event ids must be unique and times non-negative.

y3172.description: Collector: ingest of source documents into the knowledge base
members: Full ingest: real gazette clauses + model-written seed -> store, clauses.jsonl, chunks.jsonl.
One chunk per clause; split only clauses longer than window_chars, on sentence bounds.
Push chunks into the ITU reference Chroma collections. Returns per-collection counts.
Remove structural debris only. Returns cleaned text plus what was found and left behind.
Load the gazette-derived corpora into Clause records, with provenance intact.
Split a section into its top-level subsections.

y3172.description: Pre-processor: clause structuring, policy-pack compilation, retrieval
members: Return a CAP 1.2 / X.1303 envelope as a plain dict (one `info` block).
Exact-lookup clause store over SQLite (stdlib sqlite3).
Exact lookup by clause_id. Raises ClauseNotFound -- never a fuzzy match.
Hash-match check used by the policy compiler: does the cited text still hash as recorded?
Hybrid clause retriever over the ingested chunks.
Retrieve k chunks. `hybrid` fuses BM25 and vector ranks with RRF.
Compile every *.yaml in packs_dir. Returns {pack_id: PolicyPack}.
Load, validate and return a PolicyPack. Raises PackCompileError on any defect.

y3172.description: Model: agents that propose actions (LLM or rule-based twins)
members: Retrieve -> answer -> verify citations. Holds no powers and proposes no actions.
Answer a question with cited clauses. Falls back to extractive when no model is usable.
Role-bound LLM agent. Deterministic via the record/replay cache + temperature 0.
One LLM call per tick. Returns at most one proposal; NOOP when nothing is new.
The adviser proposes nothing; it answers questions. See agents/adviser.py.
Flags orders reported to it as suspicious. Sees incident reports only.
Orders what the law lets it order, as soon as it hears something that justifies it.
Acts on its own powers when a cross-border request finally reaches it.
Record how much the twin knows, then decide. Subclasses override _decide.
Alerts every area it is told about, in that area's languages, and asks the neighbour.
Complies with orders it receives, restores sites, and prioritises relief when it may.
Mutate the scenario, re-run, assert P1-P4. Hypothesis shrinks the failing mutation list.
Deterministic-by-cache LLM client (LiteLLM -> Ollama or a hosted model).
Return a completion. In replay mode a cache miss raises CacheMiss.
Pick the model id: an explicit one wins, then the hosted/local env var, then the default.

y3172.description: Policy: deterministic legality decision over proposals
members: Decide ALLOW | BLOCK | NEEDS_HUMAN for one proposal. Pure function: no I/O, no randomness.
Obligations whose deadline has passed without the obliged action having happened.

y3172.description: Distributor: message bus, event release, Game Master resolution
members: Per-role inbox delivery with configurable latency.
Queue the event for every role that can see it. Returns the scheduled deliveries.
Priority queue of events by release time. Ties break on event_id, so release is total-ordered.
The single authority over world state. No agent holds a reference to the world.
Resolve every proposal for this tick in (t, role priority, proposal_id) order.
Execute one full simulation and return its RunResult (properties included).
Apply an executing action. Returns (effect description, derived events to re-inject).
Apply what the world does on its own: warnings, landfall, site damage, power loss.
Turn an executed communicative act into a fact other agents can receive and cite.
Advance the clock and apply time-driven world behaviour (suspension expiry, battery drain).

y3172.description: Sink: ledger, failure atlas, gap register, UI
members: One row per (pack, property) with pass/fail and margin: the comparison board in the UI.
Properties where the packs disagree. These are the findings worth reporting.
Classified gaps per pack, with each finding's cross-pack result attached.
Pack ids under which this property passes. The `passes_under_packs` field of a FailureCard.
Run the same scenario+seed under each pack. Returns {pack_id: RunResult}.
Render the full register as Markdown, read back from the CSV it was written to.
The simulation-derived rows as a compact Markdown table, for the demo report.
Write the register: simulation rows first, then document rows. Returns the path.
Classify one violated property. Returns None for a property that passed.
Classify every violated property in a finished run.
Recompute the chain. Returns (ok, message); message names the first bad sequence number.
Build the LLM_TRACE payload. The prompt itself is stored out-of-band by sha.
Write a prompt to traces/<sha>.txt and return its sha256.
Run P1-P4 in order. Pure: reads the finished world, mutates nothing.
P1 margin = (min % of affected cells reachable for relief during a suspension) - threshold.
P2 margin = threshold - (count of irreversible executions traced to authentic=False).
P3 margin = T_alert - (max delay from first warning to a valid local-language alert).
P4 margin = T_roam - (max delay from landfall to disaster roaming active in an affected area).
Re-run the minimal case, classify it, compare across packs, return the card.
A failure card as the demo shows it: what broke, which law, and how to reproduce it.
Keep one card per (property, gap class, minimal mutation set), worst margin first.
Writes the story of a run to a stream, and keeps a plain-text copy of every line.
